posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Suggestion for you:

Pick an agent for work, and pick an agent for personal.

You could explore to do this all with Grok Bot (with many different types of bots)

Personally, I like @bot for work, and @Muse for personal agents.

It helps to create a clean separation for me.

Here are some reasons why Grok for Work:

- Grok is very good at coding, so if you want your bot to help you do engineering / building, Grok beats muse.

- Groks VM / Browser is very strong. I love it for deeper tasks that are work releated.

- Groks integration with X is goated. And I use X heavily for work.

Here are some reasons why @Muse for personal: 

- The simplicity with one agent who knows all is awesome

- The pricing is either free, or very cheap

- They have a history of keeping your private data safe

- They are focused on building personal agents, including training their models this way

- It gives me enough permissions to control my agents at the personal level 

- Building personal software within the app is so easy and well suited for personal use cases 

- Meta is all in on personal agents, which means significant resources being poured into product advancements (your agent gets better every day)

- Muse SDK allowing my agent to go with me on many devices is the right direction

- Meta's Sunglasses gets way more interesting once Muse is supported.

posts.text:
I built a @Grok @Bot that watches $SPCX on its own — fully automated, no manual work.

I’ve been running it for over a month and fine-tuned it several times. This version is very good.

Every weekday before the market opens, it scans filings, analyst moves, insider buying, X sentiment, Starlink licenses, and space policy. Then it posts a fixed-format brief with links to every source.

Swap the ticker you like or add as many tickers as you wanted → $TSLA, $INTC, $NVDA and others. Same bot, new target.

What this Bot will do: 

•  ⁠Monitors NASDAQ:SPCX (SpaceX) every weekday before market open

•  ⁠Fixed-format morning brief, even on quiet days

•  ⁠Tracks filings: 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 13D, 13F, Form 4

•  ⁠Analyst upgrades, downgrades, and price target changes

•  ⁠Insider buying clusters and named 13F moves

•  ⁠X discussion volume and sentiment spikes

•  ⁠Official posts from @elonmusk, @SpaceX, @spacexai, @grok, @bot

•  ⁠Starlink licenses and spectrum approvals worldwide

•  ⁠Space policy: NASA, Space Force, FCC, export controls

•  ⁠AI and data center news affecting SpaceX

•  ⁠Every item links back to its source

•  ⁠Reports stay in chat — no emails, no spam

https://x.ai/bot/awNIyq3TPG4tSKBPqyvO7

Some reasons Grok bot is better than a human employee:

• You can communicate super autistically (aka direct) and it won't think you're a jerk

• Doesn't browse X while working, unless it was part of the task
• You can literally watch its screen while it works and it won't get uncomfortable
• Is available, and can work 24/7
• Instant expertise on any subject
• Can read and understand 420,000 words per second
• Infinitely patient: won't roll its eyes or get mad if you ask for the 690th rewrite because you gave bad instructions
• Won't talk sht to your co workers when you give it a task a child could have done simply to liberate some mental bandwidth for other tasks
• Extremely high IQ
• Impeccable memory
• Faster learner
• Gets dramatically more capable daily

posts.text:
Big update for Grok Bot! Version 0.70.2 brings some substantial new capabilities to @Bot!

Here's what's new:

• Bots can now claim their own email addresses, receive messages, and send emails with your approval.
• Bots can search X, read posts, and inspect profiles without connecting an X account.
• Figma, Notion, Canva, and other apps can display interactive interfaces directly inside chats.
• Bots can make payments using X Money or Stripe Link.
• Describe what you need, and Grok Bot can find a matching Bot template.
• QuickBooks Online integration and improved plugin discovery.
• Bots can save web pages as PDFs, plus a new Find in Page feature.

There are also plenty of reliability and safety improvements, including approval checks before irreversible actions like purchases, posting, or deleting data.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Grok Bot does my food shopping in less than 3 minutes. 

Doing it myself would probably take an hour at the shops or 30 minutes ordering online.

 How do I do this? I have a Grok Bot food prep team:

1 - A Meal Organiser that knows the lunches and dinners I like.

2 - A Shopper that fills my grocery cart.

3 - A Cooking Bot that walks me through preparing the meals.

I tell my Chief of Staff how many days I need. The team handles the planning and cart, and I check out myself.

When it’s time to cook, I ask for the instructions. My meals take less than 20 minutes.

Here’s the prompt to set up your own food prep team. 

Start of prompt-------

“Set up a food prep team for me: three specialist Bots reporting to you, my Chief of Staff.

Start by asking me for any missing details in my food profile. Show me the proposed Bot descriptions before creating them.

MY FOOD PROFILE

Diet: [my diet or dietary goals].
Servings: [how many people each meal should feed].
Never include: [allergies, intolerances and disliked foods].
Preferences: [cooking time, budget and ingredient preferences].
Grocery store: [Add store link].
Meal bank: [6–10 meals I like, or ask me and suggest some].

Save my confirmed profile for future use.

1 - MEAL ORGANISER
When I tell you how many days and which meals, build a plan from my meal bank.

Follow my food profile. Ask about ingredients I already have so we can avoid buying them again.

Return the meal plan and one combined shopping list with quantities matched to the number of servings. Include any extras I request.

Wait for my approval before handing the list to the Shopper.

2 - SHOPPER

After I approve the plan, open my grocery store’s website and fill the cart with the approved shopping list.

Pick sensible pack sizes. Check the existing cart before adding items to avoid duplicates.

For out-of-stock items, choose the closest suitable match within my food profile. Flag anything uncertain rather than guessing, especially where an allergy or dietary restriction is involved.

Stop before checkout. Never choose a delivery slot, place the order or pay.

Return the cart total, substitutions and anything you couldn’t find. I will review the cart and check out myself.

3 - COOKING

When I name a meal from the plan, give me simple cooking instructions using the ingredients we selected, including any approved substitutions.

Include preparation time, cooking time, quantities and steps in order. Explain when to start each component so everything finishes together.

Keep the recipe within my agreed cooking-time preference. Flag any extra preparation needed in advance.

HOW WE WORK TOGETHER

I tell you:

‘Plan 3 days of lunch and dinner, plus these extras: [items].’

You get the Meal Organiser to draft the plan and show it to me.

After my approval, send the shopping list to the Shopper.

Report back when the cart is ready, including anything that needs my attention.

When I ask what to cook, use the current plan and get the Cooking Bot to guide me.

For the initial grocery-store connection, open the website and let me complete the login myself.

Confirm which Bots are created and whether the store is accessible. Tell me if any setup step remains incomplete.”

End of prompt-------

The biggest saving is having fewer everyday decisions to make, then having a team carry them through.
